who adhered to the heresy of the Maronites.
And he has a wonderful book of Chronography in Syriac,
although in it he insults and reviles the orthodox (believers).
And he translated the two books of Homer on Ilium from Greek into Syriac.
For he served the Caliph al-Mahdi,
and was greatly beloved by him on account of his pre-eminence in this art of astrology.
It is said
that on one of the days the Caliph wished to travel to one of his cities,
and his household with him.
And the wife of the Caliph sent to Theophilus, saying to him:
"You have counseled the king to travel,
and have caused us the toil and hardship of the road,
which we had no need of.
Therefore, I hope in God that He will quickly sweep you away and remove you from the earth,
so that we may rest,
being rid of you."
And this Theophilus answered the handmaid who had come to him on this embassy:
"Go back and say to your mistress:
'It is not I who counseled the Caliph to travel,
rather, he travels as he wishes.
And this curse which you have cursed me, that God should hasten my death —
already this lot had gone forth from God and been confirmed,
and quickly I shall die.
However, do not suppose that it is because your prayer was accepted that my death occurs,
rather, the will of Him who created me is being fulfilled.
Moreover, you,
O queen,
I say to you {OCR?}:
prepare for yourself much dust,
and when you hear that I am dead,
fill all that dust upon your head.'"
And when the queen heard these things, she trembled greatly,
and was watching to see what would come of this matter.
And after a few days, that Theophilus died.
And after twenty days, the Caliph al-Mahdi also died,
and that which Theophilus had decreed was brought to pass.
And in the year 190 [of the Arabs]
(1090 of the Greeks, 779
of our Lord?) al-Mahdi came to Aleppo.
And the Tanukhites who lived around Aleppo in tents came out to meet him,
riding on fine Arab horses and adorned.
Then it was told him
that all these were Christians.
And he boiled with rage,
and compelled them to embrace Islam.
And about five thousand men embraced Islam,
the women, however, escaped.
